previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis and Child-Pugh class B cirrhosis was admitted for acute epigastric and right upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the back, associated with low-grade fever and nausea. Imaging showed stable cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and retained biliary stones without evidence of acute pancreatitis or cholangitis. A single blood culture grew coagulase-negative staph, interpreted as a contaminant; vancomycin was briefly administered and discontinued. Hypoxia noted in the ED resolved and was attributed to opioid use. Her pain improved with conservative management, and she was discharged home on her baseline medications with instructions to monitor for recurrent symptoms and follow up for transplant evaluation and repeat EGD.

============================
BRIEF SUMMARY:
============================
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old woman with PSC c/b Childs B 
Cirrhosis, on transplant list, approved for living donor 
transplant, with history of ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, and 
small to medium sized varices s/p banding on ___, and 
recurrent cholangitis with no positive culture data, who 
presented with fevers and worsening abdominal pain concerning 
for cholangitis, with subsequent response in fevers on meropenem 
(c/w prior history) and PICC line placement for completion of 
ertapenem based outpatient antibiotics for a 2 week course w/ 
___ services.

============================
DETAILED SUMMARY BY PROBLEM: 
============================
#Acute cholangitis:  Patient has a history of recurrent 
cholangitis, never presenting with any positive cultures.  She 
presented to the hospital with fevers and abdominal pain 
concerning for recurrence, she was found to have elevated liver 
enzymes and bilirubin.  She was started on treatment with 
meropenem, given that this was the only antibiotic that had 
helped her during past episodes of this recurrent cholangitis.   
Blood cultures returned negative for bacteria, therefore past 
responsiveness was used to guide therapy. A PICC line was placed 
in order to continue outpatient parenteral antibiotics.  As she 
transitioned to discharge, meropenem was replaced with ertapenem 
to facilitate outpatient ___ service antibiotic administration.  
Course was scheduled to end on ___.

#C. difficile:  after initial dosing of meropenem, patient began 
to experience profuse diarrhea.  C. difficile toxin was sent for 
identification, and returned positive morning of ___.  She was 
started on vancomycin 125 mg 4 times a day course,  which will 
continue until her transplant date or until specified otherwise 
by the transplant hepatologists.

___:   patient presented with evidence of acute kidney injury, 
with a creatinine of approximately 0.9 from a baseline of around 
0.5. She was resuscitated with IV fluids and she returned to her 
baseline, likely demonstrating a prerenal picture of acute 
kidney injury, most likely secondary to poor oral intake.

#PSC c/b Child's B cirrhosis (h/o ascites, HE, varices):  
Patient's home diuretics were held in the setting of a possible 
acute infection.  On discharge she was restarted on 40 mg of 
Lasix and 100 mg of spironolactone daily.  She had recently been 
approved along with her donor for a living donor liver 
transplant.  As such her antibiotic course and C. difficile 
treatment were planned in accordance with preparing her for her 
upcoming transplant.  Her home ursodiol, cholestyramine, and 
rifaximin were continued without issue.

EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  History: ___ with PSC p/w worsening RUQ pain, fever  // ? portal
vein patency

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The liver is coarsened and nodular in echotexture. The contour of the
liver is nodular, consistent with cirrhosis. There is no focal liver mass. The
main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow. There is no appreciable
ascites.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CHD measures 4 mm.

GALLBLADDER:  Patient is status post cholecystectomy.  Echogenic foci within
the gallbladder remnant resultant shadowing in the gallbladder fossa, similar
to prior examinations.

PANCREAS: The pancreas is not well visualized, largely obscured by overlying
bowel gas.

SPLEEN:  The spleen is enlarged, measuring 16.5 cm, previously 15.4 cm.

KIDNEYS:  Limited views of the right kidney show no hydronephrosis.

RETROPERITONEUM:  The visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Coarsened and nodular liver in keeping with history of cirrhosis. 
Splenomegaly, minimally increased relative to prior study, without appreciable
ascites.

2.  Retained gallstones within the gallbladder remnant, unchanged.

3.  No intra or extrahepatic duct dilation.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with liver disease and cholangitis requiring ___
guided PICC, has had trouble with bedside piccs in the past patient requesting
___ Picc placement.

COMPARISON:  None.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ and Dr.
___ radiologist performed the procedure. Dr. ___
supervised the trainee during the key components of the procedure and has
reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: 1% lidocaine was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues
overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: 1% lidocaine.
CONTRAST: 0 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  1.3 min, 2 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. Single lumen PICC placement through the right basilic vein.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right
basilic vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a
micropuncture set. Permanent ultrasound images were obtained before and after
intravenous access, which confirmed vein patency. A peel-away sheath was then
placed over a guidewire. The guidewire was then advanced into the superior
vena cava using fluoroscopic guidance. A single lumen PIC line measuring 35 cm
in length was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned
in the distal SVC under fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the catheter was
confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest. The peel-away sheath and
guidewire were then removed. The catheter was secured to the skin, flushed,
and a sterile dressing applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS: 

1.  The accessed vein was patent and compressible.
2.  Basilicvein approach single lumen right PICC with tip in the distal SVC.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a right 35 cm basilic approach single lumen PowerPICC
with tip in the distal SVC.  The line is ready to use.
